subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should local avatar failures keep the current generic direct-route 404 and only improve authenticated UI diagnostics, or should `/avatar/{agentId}` itself expose more specific failure statuses for oversized, missing, or rejected files?
rationale: The remaining behavior sits on an authenticated local workspace file-serving path, so more detailed endpoint errors could improve UX but also change information-disclosure boundaries.

options.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using the existing metadata reason and Quick Settings/chat surfaces to show clear oversized or missing-file guidance.

options.title: Expose Endpoint Errors
options.body: Return more specific statuses such as 413 or 400 from the direct avatar route, with explicit security review and tests proving no unsafe path details leak.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Avatar Contract
options.body: Defer this local diagnostics decision into the broader remote/local avatar contract tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41201.

recommendation.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using the existing metadata reason and Quick Settings/chat surfaces to show clear oversized or missing-file guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties the original avatar feature and subsequent local avatar safety hardening to this owner path.
